exposure: Complications during cesarean section (Unpacking, Obstetric hemorrhage, Bleeding due to uterine atony, Hysterotomy commissure hematoma, Uterine infiltration, Vascular injury, Bladder injury, Colonic injury)
cohort: The study included 3371 patients who underwent cesarean section at the Toco-Surgical Unit of the Gynecological Obstetrics Hospital No. 3 of the National Medical Center "La Raza" Mexican Institute of Social Security from January to December 2019.
finding: The prevalence of surgical reintervention due to complications after cesarean section was 1.60%, with bleeding being the main cause, and the clinical evolution was satisfactory with low mortality (1.85%).
mod_finding: Surgical reintervention due to complications during cesarean section occurred in 1.60% of patients, primarily caused by bleeding (unpacking, obstetric hemorrhage, uterine atony, hysterotomy commissure hematoma).
